injuries.description: right wrist sprain with contusion triquetral bone and triangular fibrocartilage focal perforation; chronic tear of the scapho-lunate (SL) ligament with osteochondral lesion of distal radius (right wrist)
source: As a result of the Accident, the Plaintiff suffered minor neck sprain with soft tissue injury, right wrist sprain with contusion triquetral bone/triangular fibrocartilage focal perforation, and bilateral knee contusion with partial tear of ACL on left side.

The results showed chronic tear of the SL ligament with instability of the SL joint together with an osteochrondal lesion over the distal radius articular surface. Debridement of the tears was performed, and the Plaintiff was discharged on the same day.

After discussion about the option of continuing conservative treatment or operative reconstruction of the wrist lesions, the Plaintiff preferred the latter. He continued with hand therapy/training until the surgery on 27 May 2008 which consisted of arthroscopy of the right wrist, reconstruction of the SL ligament with tendon graft, K wire fixation and osteochondral graft transfer from the left knee to restore the osteochrondral defect of the right wrist.

injuries.description: bilateral knee contusion with partial tear of ACL on left side
source: As a result of the Accident, the Plaintiff suffered minor neck sprain with soft tissue injury, right wrist sprain with contusion triquetral bone/triangular fibrocartilage focal perforation, and bilateral knee contusion with partial tear of ACL on left side.

OMDC’s radiologist Dr Simon Le reported on the MRI films of the left knee that there was partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) with a small left knee joint effusion, but the posterior cruciate/collateral ligaments and menisci were intact with no tear.

According to the Discharge Slip, the relevant procedures done on 28 January 2010 were "[arthroscopy] of knee (Left. Diagnostic) …… Lateral release knee (Open) …… Chondroplasty of knee (Artificial Osteochondral plug implantation …...)".
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of anterior cruciate ligament of knee, excluding rupture

manifestations.description: on-and-off right wrist pain, increases with prolonged writing; pain on exertion
limited right wrist range of motion (extension up to 20°, flexion 30°)
swelling and diffuse tenderness over right wrist (maximal at radial styloid)
cannot lift weight over 3kg with right hand
bilateral knee pain (worse in left), walking tolerance 15-30 minutes (if using knee support), cannot squat fully
mild tenderness at lateral patella facet of both knees (more on left)
neck tenderness / neck pain from sprain

treatments_received: Emergency treatment at Queen Elizabeth Hospital: wound dressing, suture and analgesics
Physiotherapy at Prime Rehabilitation Services (2 sessions per week)
Arthroscopy of right wrist and reconstruction of SL ligament with tendon graft, K wire fixation and osteochondral graft transfer from left knee (27 May 2008)
Physiotherapy and occupational therapy at Prince of Wales Hospital
Left knee arthroscopy and chondroplasty / lateral release / artificial osteochondral plug implantation (hospitalised 27 January to 3 February 2010)

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Gave up vigorous sports after the Accident (soccer, rowing, dragon boat, marathon and Trailwalker); stopped motorcycle riding
Restriction of social circle due to inability to play soccer and participate in sports
Plaintiff became depressed and reticent; claims matrimonial relationship adversely affected and wife has lived separately from him since the end of 2007
Reduced walking tolerance (15-30 minutes without support), inability to squat fully; requires knee brace for stability
